company.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
company.about: Ratnaveer makes austenitic stainless-steel products in Vadodara, Gujarat: finishing sheets, washers, pipes and tubes, and roofing hooks for solar mounting systems, sold to industrial and solar customers in India and abroad. It is building a copper-clad laminate (CCL) plant, the base material for printed circuit boards, backed by approval under the central government's electronics component scheme.
highlights: CCL plant trial run due Dec 2026

events.title: Stock sets a record near ₹359, about 2.7x its March low, then slips 7% without news
events.details: Ratnaveer shares made a series of record highs in October 2026, with aggregators putting the peak at about ₹358–360 (an intraday ₹358.80 on 19 October). That was roughly 2.7 times the 52-week low of about ₹130 in late March. The stock then fell about 7% with no company announcement, closing at ₹335.10 on 21 October and trading near ₹326.50 on 22 October. At ₹344 on 9 October it traded at about 43 times trailing earnings, roughly double its three-year average multiple.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the price now sits above the only named broker target and assumes the copper-clad laminate project succeeds, so execution news can move it sharply.

events.title: Kingboard raises thin-glass laminate prices 15%, reportedly its eighth increase of 2026
events.details: Kingboard, one of the largest global makers of copper-clad laminate, raised prices on thin-glass laminate and prepreg by about 15% on 13 October 2026. An industry note said it was the company's eighth increase this year and that no new glass-cloth capacity is expected before the end of 2027. Ratnaveer's laminate plan rests on replacing imports while Chinese supply is tight: more than 90% of Indian demand is imported and laminate prices have roughly tripled.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: tight supply should help pricing when Ratnaveer's first laminate line starts, but the company also imports glass fabric, so its input costs rise too.

events.title: Investor Nileshkumar Farshuram HUF sells 8 lakh shares at ₹340
events.details: Nileshkumar Farshuram HUF sold 8 lakh Ratnaveer shares at ₹340 each, about ₹27 crore, in a bulk deal around 7 October 2026. It followed bulk-deal exits by several trading firms after the rights shares listed in mid-September, including Crabel Vintrade and Golden Goenka on 28 September and Arihant Capital on 5 October. The buyers were not identified in the coverage found.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: steady selling by short-term holders near record highs is a sign of profit-taking rather than a fundamental change.

events.title: Shanti Gold International buys a 0.37% stake for ₹8.83 Cr at about ₹333 a share
events.details: Shanti Gold International bought about 2.65 lakh Ratnaveer shares, roughly 0.37% of the company, in the open market on 26 September 2026 at an average price of ₹333.33, for about ₹8.83 crore. The same day the company held its 24th annual general meeting by video conference, covering the accounts, borrowing limits, auditor re-appointment and a director appointment; the scrutinizer's report was filed on 28 September.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a small open-market purchase near record prices; it adds little beyond sentiment.

events.title: CCL plant update: order bookings from 31 Oct, trial run in Dec, launch mid-Jan 2027
events.details: Ratnaveer said order bookings for its copper-clad laminate plant in Vadodara would start on 31 October 2026, with trial production in the second week of December and an inauguration around mid-January 2027. In July the company had pointed to commercial production in November 2026, so the schedule has slipped by about one to two months. The first phase is planned at 15.84 lakh sheets a year, about ₹108 crore of revenue; full scale is 79.2 lakh sheets and ₹750 crore or more. The stock saw a record ₹472 crore of turnover that day.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the laminate plant is central to the valuation, so even small delays matter; revenue is not expected before the March 2027 quarter.

events.title: Allots ₹330 Cr of rights shares at ₹264; promoters skip the issue and their stake falls to 38.7%
events.details: Ratnaveer allotted 1,24,99,669 rights shares at ₹264 each, raising ₹329.99 crore, after an issue that was open from 2 to 9 September and was reported as subscribed about 1.11 times. Shares outstanding rose to 8,39,26,350, about 17.5% more. The promoter group did not take up its entitlement, so its holding fell from 45.49% in June to 38.71% in September; foreign investors' holding rose to about 7.5%. The rights shares listed on 15 September. About ₹255 crore is for working capital and the rest for the laminate project.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the cash eases working-capital strain, but promoters not investing alongside shareholders, and a falling promoter stake, are worth watching.

events.title: ICICI Direct reiterates Buy and raises target to ₹325, from ₹255
events.details: ICICI Direct, the retail research arm of ICICI Securities and the only named broker covering the stock, issued a company update with a Buy rating and a ₹325 target. Its target had been ₹235 in May 2026 and ₹255 in July, which the stock had already passed. The update followed the Q1 FY27 results and the rights-issue terms. By October the share price was trading above the new target.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: coverage is thin, so a single broker's view carries weight; the price running past the target shows momentum ahead of fundamentals.

events.title: Board fixes ₹330 Cr rights issue at ₹264 a share (7 for 40); stock hits a record ₹282.50
events.details: The board set the terms of its rights issue: 1,24,99,669 shares at ₹264 each, including a ₹254 premium, in the ratio of 7 new shares for every 40 held, with a record date of 26 August 2026. The issue had first been approved on 11 June for up to ₹330 crore and received NSE and BSE in-principle approval on 17 July. The shares touched a then all-time high of ₹282.50 around the announcement, having risen steadily since the Q1 results.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: pricing the issue at a discount to market eased take-up, but it was the fourth equity raise in about two years.

events.title: Stock hits a fresh 52-week high of ₹223.75, up about 25% in a month
events.details: Ratnaveer shares touched a 52-week high of ₹223.75 on 14 August 2026, after an earlier high of ₹215.75 on 4 August, and were up about 24.65% over the previous month. The rally began with the 10% upper circuit after the Q1 FY27 results in late July and continued on news about the copper-clad laminate plant and the pending rights issue. The stock had traded sideways between about ₹135 and ₹180 from November 2025 to July 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: this was the start of a move that more than doubled the price in under three months.

events.title: Q1 FY27: revenue up 19% to ₹315 Cr, PAT up 22% to ₹18.2 Cr; stock hits 10% upper circuit
events.details: For the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 18.9% year on year to ₹314.6 crore and profit after tax rose about 22% to ₹18.2 crore. Operating EBITDA grew 19.1% to ₹32.2 crore, a 10.2% margin. Finance costs roughly doubled to ₹6.72 crore. The company also reported the copper-clad laminate project about 60% complete and in-principle exchange approval for the rights issue. The shares hit their 10% upper circuit after the results.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a solid quarter, but growth and margins were below the FY27 guidance of more than 25% growth, 13% EBITDA margin and 9% net margin.

events.title: Management guides FY27 revenue of ₹1,350 Cr with 13% EBITDA margin; targets ₹2,500 Cr in 2–3 years
events.details: On the Q4 FY26 earnings call, management guided for FY27 revenue of about ₹1,350 crore, more than 25% growth, with capacity use around 80%, an EBITDA margin of 13% and a net margin of 9%. It said the laminate business could reach about ₹750 crore at full scale, taking consolidated revenue to about ₹2,500 crore in two to three years. FY26 capex was about ₹115 crore, and further stainless-steel expansion is planned. The call also flagged negative operating cash flow.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the guidance implies a sharp margin step-up from about 10.5%; early FY27 quarters have tracked below it.

events.title: FY26: revenue up 20% to ₹1,069 Cr, PAT up 37% to ₹64.3 Cr; Q4 profit up 59%
events.details: Consolidated revenue for FY26 rose about 20% to ₹1,068.7 crore and profit after tax rose 37% to ₹64.3 crore. In the March 2026 quarter, revenue from operations rose 22.6% to ₹249.0 crore and profit after tax rose 59% to ₹17.03 crore, roughly flat on the previous quarter. EBITDA margin for the year improved to about 10.5% from 9.7%. FY26 revenue slightly beat the company's earlier target of about ₹1,050 crore. The shares rose about 7% after the results.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: profit is growing faster than revenue as margins improve, but cash flow from operations was negative for the year.

events.title: Infomerics upgrades credit rating to IVR A-/Stable from BBB+; rated facilities raised to ₹388 Cr
events.details: Infomerics Valuation and Rating upgraded Ratnaveer's long-term bank facilities to IVR A-/Stable from IVR BBB+/Positive, and its short-term rating to IVR A2+ from IVR A2, by a letter dated 23 April 2026. The company disclosed it on 24 April. The total rated bank facilities were raised to ₹388.47 crore from ₹295.76 crore. The company cited better operating performance, financial strength and execution.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a higher rating lowers borrowing costs for a business that relies heavily on working-capital credit.

events.title: Wins central ECMS approval for a ₹338 Cr copper-clad laminate plant in Vadodara
events.details: Ratnaveer received approval under the government's Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme for a copper-clad laminate project in Vadodara, with planned investment of about ₹338 crore over three years and five production lines. Managing Director Vijay Sanghavi received the letter from Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in New Delhi on 30 March 2026. A larger ₹472.34 crore version has in-principle approval under the Gujarat Electronics Policy. The company described it as India's first integrated laminate plant; more than 90% of Indian demand is imported.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the project moves the company into electronics materials, which is why the stock re-rated, but it has no revenue yet and depends on subsidies and high import prices.

events.title: Q3 FY26: PAT up 50% to ₹16.9 Cr on 6% revenue growth as EBITDA margin widens to 10.6%
events.details: For the December 2025 quarter, revenue rose about 5.8% year on year to ₹269.3 crore, while profit after tax rose 49.6% to ₹16.9 crore. EBITDA rose 38.6% to ₹28.6 crore and the margin widened to 10.6% from 8.1% a year earlier. The company also filed a monitoring agency report showing no deviation in the use of the December QIP money. Revenue was lower than in the September quarter.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: margin gains drove profit, but slower revenue growth raised questions about demand in the stainless business.

events.title: Board approves 72.3 lakh promoter warrants at ₹159 (~₹115 Cr) and converts earlier warrants at ₹143
events.details: The board allotted 20,27,972 shares at ₹143 to promoter Vijay Sanghavi on conversion of warrants issued in 2024, when the company had also placed 45.5 lakh shares at ₹143 with non-promoter investors. It also approved issuing 72,32,704 new warrants at ₹159 each, about ₹115 crore, to Vijay Sanghavi, Seema Sanghavi and Ratnaveer Ventures, convertible within 18 months. After shareholder approval at an EGM, the warrants were allotted in March 2026 at ₹159.25; about 34.3 lakh had been converted by May.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: promoters adding money is a show of confidence, but warrants priced near ₹159 were well below the later market price.

events.title: Raises ₹185.5 Cr through a QIP at ₹145 a share, below the ₹211 Cr maximum
events.details: Ratnaveer opened a qualified institutional placement on 1 December 2025 with a floor price of ₹152.46 and a target of up to ₹211 crore, including a green-shoe option. It closed on 4 December with 1,27,93,102 shares allotted at ₹145, a 4.89% discount to the floor, raising about ₹185.5 crore. The money was earmarked for working capital and general corporate purposes. Astorne Capital, one of the allottees, later sold part of its stake.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the issue raised less than planned and at a discount, and it was the first of three equity raises within ten months.

events.title: Q2 FY26: revenue ₹286 Cr, PAT ₹15.4 Cr, both up about a quarter year on year
events.details: For the September 2025 quarter, revenue was ₹285.9 crore and profit after tax ₹15.4 crore, against net sales of about ₹230 crore and profit of about ₹12.3 crore a year earlier, growth of roughly a quarter on both lines. EBITDA was ₹28.3 crore, a 9.9% margin. Earnings per share were ₹3.07. It was the highest quarterly revenue of FY26; the next two quarters were lower.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: steady growth, but without the margin expansion that came later in the year.

events.title: FY25: sales up 50% to ₹892 Cr and profit up 51% to ₹46.8 Cr; Q4 profit nearly doubles
events.details: For FY25, sales rose 49.8% to ₹891.9 crore and net profit rose 50.8% to ₹46.8 crore, with earnings per share of ₹9.31. In the March 2025 quarter, sales were ₹203.1 crore and net profit ₹10.7 crore, up 90.9%. The company attributed growth to higher volumes, cost control and new markets. No dividend was declared. Reported EBITDA definitions differ between sources, at about ₹86–90 crore.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: strong growth in the first full year after listing set the base for the FY26–FY27 expansion plans.

events.title: EGM drops planned preferential issue as company says it does not need the money for now
events.details: In November 2024 the board had proposed raising funds through a private placement of shares and convertible warrants to promoters and others. At an EGM on 10 December 2024 the company withdrew the plan, saying it did not currently need to raise funds on a preferential basis because some upcoming projects had been postponed, so it also did not need to raise its authorised capital. A year later it raised equity through a QIP instead.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the reversal showed changing capital plans, a pattern repeated in later fund-raising.

events.title: Stock jumps 19% to a record ₹266.90, up 47% in five days on results and ₹180 Cr of orders
events.details: Ratnaveer shares rose as much as 19% to a then record ₹266.90 on 22 November 2024 on heavy volume, taking the five-day gain to 47%. September-quarter results showed net sales up 61.4% to about ₹230 crore and profit up 54% to about ₹12.3 crore. The company said it had orders of about ₹180 crore to execute over three to four months, was targeting defence work for its pipes division, and that phase-one capex was 80% complete with operations expected from 1 January 2025.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the spike set a high that the stock did not regain until August 2026.

events.title: Lists at ₹123.20 on NSE, a 26% premium to the ₹98 IPO price, after 94x subscription
events.details: Ratnaveer's shares began trading on 11 September 2023 after an IPO priced at the top of its ₹93–98 band. The issue was subscribed 93.99 times overall, with the institutional portion subscribed 133 times. The stock opened at ₹123.20 on NSE, about 26% above the issue price, and at ₹128 on BSE, about 31% higher. It dipped after the open and then rose to ₹134.40 during the first session, 37% above the IPO price.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: strong demand at listing gave the company a currency for the repeated equity raises that followed.
